title: Misleading description: not a submarine strategy game.
body: The description and screen shots are all about submarine combat. As many other reviewers point out, this is a very minor part of the game. I actually enjoyed the main game for a time, building up my “base,” researching technology, gathering resources, battling “invaders,” etc. Oh, and sometimes participating in the very basic submarine aspect. Even the main gameplay is very repetitive. You basically do the same things over and over, with some “events” that cycle through from time to time. Although, it is sort of meditative. I enjoyed logging in for an hour or so in the evening, going through the events, building stockpiles to create buildings, units, etc. The main problem I had was that after reaching a certain point (level 25 base, nearly VIP 10 in my case) you are subject to almost continuous attack by much more advanced players. This isn’t a problem if you are online and can be proactive, but the game allows players to attack and pillage your resources when you are not online. You log off thinking “job well done” and the next time you log in your base is on fire and your stuff is gone. So, all the time spent preparing for a major building upgrade or research project down the tubes, start over (or pay big $$$ to replace the stolen resources). I contacted the developer about options and was told “it’s a war game. If you don’t want to be attacked when you’re not online use (the temporary and costly) shields.” This isn’t fun anymore. I’m out. Deleting app. UPDATE: I commend the developer for responding to negative reviews and offering to consider suggestions. However, I had reached out directly via the in-app customer service chat before posting my review, and got the exact (cut and paste) response as here. The response to my suggestion that there be an option to limit being pillaged while offline yielded the response above. For those who can dedicate a lot of time to the game, get fully immersed in the guilds, missions, etc., this may be a great game. For those of us who are more casual players, or those looking for a naval/submarine strategy game, this is not it.

title: Fun game, but not as advertised
body: This is a fun and addicting game, but frustrating at the same time. The sub and naval portion of the game that is advertised is simply a non-contributing side mission style portion of the actual game itself. It would take very little to make the submarine portion of this game earn rewards as you do with all other side missions in this game, but alas, it was not that way while I was there. You can develop battleships that are deployed with your marching troops to increase certain buffs and strengths, but this is 100% a land focused war strategy game, do not get fooled if that’s not what you’re looking for. Also, you can and will grow without spending money; however, you need to understand that somewhere around HQ level 19-23, it will become extremely apparent as to who is spending money and who is not. Those who are not can still have fun, but you will likely be funneled into more of a guild “support” role as many of the missions, rally’s etc. simply operate better when higher ranked individuals lead them, and if you’re not spending money - you’re not that guy…trust me. Lastly, customer service response time is horrible, beyond horrible. I’m talking, must be one person fielding all the customer service responses, and I’m assuming this is his or hers side gig. The most common and likely responses you will be prompted with when submitting a question, concern, or request for help is either, we are fielding a large number of customer service requests at this time and will get back to you as soon as possible (which can be 24-48 hrs), or they force close your request and simply say that because you didn’t respond to something your request has been closed, even though you had no questions from their team to respond to originally. Game itself, knowing it’s not as advertised is still a 4 out of 5, not being as advertised 1 out of 5 (0 not available), customer service response time (-10 out of 5)

title: Lost and abandoned
body: This game can (and mostly is) very interesting. It can easily pull you and captivate you. You are able to develop some wonderful contacts and new friends from around the world. However, if you happen to begin on a dead or “test” server, then your experience will turn from fun to frustration. I began on a server (296), developed a stronger player / base. Unfortunately, I was assigned to the server as a “newbie” after nearly everyone on the server had weeks, if not months, of playing time ahead of me. That being said, I never was accepted and developed connections within the server. I thought that the Transfer Order option perfectly fit my situation. But… and here is the HUGE CATCH… I am NOT ALLOWED to transfer. The developers have decided that this server (296) and a handful of others are deemed test servers. Non of us may leave the server / zone. We are trapped and our game is become boring beyond words. I have invested money in this game and was very optimistic, but when the official word came down that we can never leave, it destroyed any hope for fun. If you chose to play this game, then be aware you may become trapped in a dead game.

body: I was sucked in to this game called “Sea War.” However, it is actually a cool game called Kiss of War with a steam-punkish, mid-20th century “pin-up” vibe. Don’t get me wrong - it’s fun and engaging. You can advance (albeit VERY slowly) without purchasing anything. Pros: great strategy, fun resource management, base development game, simple but entertaining combat system, really fun mini-games. Cons: the naval combat that got me to download is a very, very small part of the game and becomes less available as the game goes on. You only get to play the submarine “shooter” game for a handful of times after each base upgrade. And those become a real grind after a couple days - it can take weeks. So if you got reeled in by an FPS or naval combat game, just realize it is only a rare mini game within a resource management sim. Which is a serious bummer. It would take very little to make this a more significant part of the game and should be considered by the developers as the advertising for the game is quite misleading. I am very deep into the game and manage a large guild on an active server at this point. Bottom line: Fun, but not as advertised at all. Can be a money pit if you are not careful.

title: Same platform, new makeup & story board
body: This game is basically the same platform (format) as Guns of Glory, Ocean War, Etc.. You have your base which you must upgrade various buildings and create troops to build your base power. The story line is kinda entertaining but a little confusing, the start of the game is slow and you can’t skip past it. The $ cost for game items if your a pay to play type is overall reasonable average packs are between 5-10$ but can go as high as 100$. Game instructions, overall game goal, even a key explaining items, troops, buffs, etc.. is non existent. The in game chat system is pretty standard & the translation feature is not too bad has issues mostly with Russian & Chinese, but other more uncommon languages like Japanese and Arabic are really quite good. Many reviews mention the women commanders in the game being to sexual or inappropriate, i don’t find this to be an issue at all. Most anime cartoons are much more sexually attired than this game. Really if your easily offended or embarrassed by pretty cartoons this is not your game, stick with Barbie’s Playhouse! Areas that could be better and contribute to more battle opportunities would be to not limit the territory that guilds can control, allow unlimited land occupation, lose the barrier walls. Doing this would put guilds into direct contact faster and force more interaction between guilds, fight, ally, etc… In addition allowing a trade system between members of the same guild and even trade between guilds. Diplomatic negotiations could be greatly expanded as well with the open territory i suggested above, where either trade relations, territorial claims be either be negotiated or fought over. There are so many opportunities to greatly improve gameplay, however most developers are focused purely on the profit potential of these types of games that improvements will most likely never come to be, even though if such improvements were made the potential profits would increase by not being like every other game and opening additional avenues for increased profit paths. In the end it’s a good game but don’t expect much more than any other game of this type.

title: Kiss of War V 1.2
body: Basically this is Kiss of War with different title and add submarine missions. You can find plenty of videos on YouTube for Kiss of War. Basic idea of the game, is build up given base, troops and resources. Take part in daily and weekly events in clans. It is a F2P game with some in game advertisement to purchase packs for the game. Level up officers, research troop, base and guild upgrades. So far servers are not as cut throat as other games, as the bigger rewards are in the bigger zone versus zone events. Server who do not work together, die off pretty quick, with players able to jump to different zone, with in power range pretty easily. With cut throat clans getting handled pretty easily in the bi-weekly zone to zone battles. If your looking for a long term game to spend time in, so far this has been great. The submarine/ship battles advertised are limited at that beginning of the game, until your able to level up your HQ to level 25 before becoming unlimited. So far there are no benefits to these battles other than wasting time and they can get fun. Fair warning pictures and videos shown in advertisements are fair stretch to the actual submarine/ship warfare. Due to this and the submarine missions have absolutely no bearing on the meat and potatoes of the game, I give it 4 stars for being sucked in, just to sink a few ships and blow up few planes.

Makes the game more enjoyable. Always check for gifts by clicking all the different icons. It is not a deal breaker but when attacking, I would like to see a limit of one or two levels below attacking commander just to make it fair for the new / weaker base commanders. Otherwise, highly recommend!!!
